# System 0.5

> System 0.5: Learning to Restore Nominal VLA Execution Under Unknown Low-Level Changes. Sangho Yun, Minsoo Kim and Hwanjo Yu (corresponding author), POSTECH. Project page: https://devsangho.github.io/System0.5-public/

System 0.5 is a learned layer between a frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policy and System 0 (the controller and the robot body). It restores each action chunk's nominal execution: the motion that the System 0 under which the policy's demonstrations were recorded would produce from the state where the chunk starts. It identifies the current System 0 from its own history of commands and measured motion and is trained by gradients through a learned forward model, without reinforcement learning. Paper and code: coming soon.

## Key results
- RoboStress joint faults (pi0.5, LIBERO): 72.7% success vs 56.6% best reported (SC-VLA); our pi0.5 base 51.8%.
- J-PARC joint-fault benchmark: 68.1% vs 61.7% best reported (J-PARC); our base 56.6%.
- Eight System 0 changes outside the training distribution (LIBERO-Spatial, 8 x 40 episodes): 84.7%, above pass-through (76.9%), rule-based gain (72.5%), rule-based + 4 modules (79.4%), APEX (76.3%) and residual SAC (42.8%).
- Training target ablation: trained toward the command, the same layer reaches 25.6%; toward the one-tick nominal response, 66.9%.
- Tracking error and success: across 11 methods, lower tracking error against the nominal execution comes with higher success (Spearman rho = -0.92).
- Real UR5e (pi0.5 fine-tuned on 29 demonstrations, pick-and-place, 30 placements per method): tracking error 9.0 mm (unit gain), 1.8 mm (online gain calibrator), 1.2 mm (System 0.5), lower at every placement; completed 16, 16 and 21 of 30; within 60 s 0, 15 and 18.

## Questions and answers
### What is System 0.5?
System 0.5 is a learned layer between a frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policy and System 0, the controller and the robot body. Once per 50 ms tick it corrects the arm part of each command so that every action chunk moves the arm as it would under the System 0 that recorded the policy's demonstrations.

### What is the nominal execution of a chunk?
The nominal execution is the trajectory that the nominal System 0, the one under which the demonstrations were recorded, would produce from the state where the chunk actually starts. It restarts from the actual state at every chunk, so the error one chunk leaves is not carried into the next.

### Why not make the arm follow the command?
Under LIBERO's own controller the hand moves about 0.22 of each commanded step per tick, and the policy learned this partial motion. Trained toward the command instead of the nominal execution, the same layer succeeds in 25.6% of episodes under changes outside its training distribution, against 76.9% for the policy without a layer.

### Does System 0.5 retrain the VLA or need the parameters of System 0?
No. The VLA stays frozen, and the layer never receives the parameters of System 0. It identifies the current System 0 from its own history of commands and measured motion, using recursive least-squares statistics and an encoder that summarizes them as a 64-dimensional vector.

### How is System 0.5 trained?
In simulation, by gradients through a learned forward model and without reinforcement learning. Training copies the simulator state at each chunk's start to record the nominal execution, and the forward model's sensitivity turns other commands into the change of motion they would cause. Training replays recorded pi0.5 chunks and never queries the VLA. At deployment one tick takes about 1 ms on one CPU thread.

### What results does System 0.5 achieve?
With pi0.5 on LIBERO, System 0.5 reaches 72.7% success on RoboStress against 56.6% best reported, and 68.1% on the J-PARC joint-fault benchmark against 61.7%. Over eight System 0 changes outside its training distribution it reaches 84.7%, above all four baselines (best 79.4%). On a real UR5e it lowers the tracking error from 9.0 to 1.2 mm at every one of 30 placements and completes 21 of 30 trials against 16 without a layer.

### Are the code and paper available?
The paper and code are coming soon. This page shows the method, the results and all 90 UR5e hardware trials.

## Abstract
A vision-language-action (VLA) policy outputs action chunks that System 0 (the controller and the robot body) turns into motion. System 0 rarely stays as it was when the demonstrations were recorded. Robots run under other controllers and gains, and joint faults can halve the success of pi0.5. A remedy that covers every change is to make the arm follow the command. In LIBERO, however, the demonstrations' System 0 moves the hand about a fifth of each commanded displacement per tick, and the policy learned this motion, not the command. We present System 0.5, a layer between a frozen VLA and System 0. The layer recovers success by learning to restore each chunk's nominal execution, the motion the demonstrations' System 0 would produce from where the chunk starts. The layer identifies the current System 0 from its own history of commands and measured motion. It is trained by gradients through a learned forward model, without reinforcement learning. With pi0.5 on LIBERO, System 0.5 exceeds the best reported success on two joint-fault benchmarks, reaching 72.7% against 56.6% on RoboStress. On average over eight changes outside its training distribution, it outperforms all four baselines. On a real UR5e, a second layer trained with the same losses lowers the tracking error from 9.0 to 1.2 mm at every one of 30 placements and completes 21 of the 30 trials against 16 without a layer.
